The total sum of the numbers 1 to 6 is 21, so P + Q + R = 21, and the sum of each pair is 7. Thus x + 6 = 7, obtaining x = 1.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: there are three overlapping circles and six square positions. From the image, the square marked 6 and the square marked x are the two intersection points of the same pair of circles. The top square and the bottom-center square are the two intersections of another pair of circles, and the left-middle square and bottom-right square are the remaining pair. Let the three pair-sums be P = x + 6, Q = top + bottom-center, and R = left-middle + bottom-right. Each circle contains two of these pair-sums, so the three circle sums are P+Q, Q+R, and R+P. Since the text requires all three circle sums to be equal, solve P+Q = Q+R = R+P, giving P = Q = R. The numbers 1 through 6 sum to 21, so P+Q+R = 21 and each pair-sum is 7. Therefore x + 6 = 7, so x = 1.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the squares labeled x and 6 both lie on the same two circles, so the third circle is the one that does not pass through either x or 6. That third circle passes through exactly the other four squares. From the text, the six numbers are 1 through 6, whose total is 21. Because every square is an intersection of two circles, each placed number is counted in exactly two circle sums. Thus the total of the three circle sums is 2 × 21 = 42. Since the three circle sums are equal, each circle must sum to 42/3 = 14. The circle avoiding x and 6 contains the other four numbers, so those other four numbers sum to 14. Therefore x + 6 is the remaining total, 21 - 14 = 7. Since 6 is already placed, x = 1.
